written.myAnswer: Centripetal force acts radially towards the centre, while instantaneous velocity is tangent to the circular path. A radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact, so the centripetal force is perpendicular to velocity.

The car experiences more centripetal force on the curve with the smaller radius. From F = mv²/r, for the same car and speed, centripetal force is inversely proportional to radius; decreasing the radius increases the force.
